entry.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter multimodal AI model optimized for Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with a 1M-token context window [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Meta has launched Muse Spark Open, a large multimodal AI model with 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, designed for complex coding and multi-step reasoning tasks. The model is optimized to run on Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios using the MLX framework, enabling powerful on-device AI capabilities for developers and researchers. Muse Spark Open is available through multiple API platforms and cloud providers, with weights downloadable from Amazon SageMaker, Google Cloud, Hugging Face, and Microsoft Foundry Models. It supports various inference engines and hardware architectures, including AMD, Apple, Intel, and NVIDIA silicon, and can be customized using PyTorch. Meta has implemented safety measures and evaluated the model against its Superintelligence Scaling Framework before release. The model is distributed under the Muse Model License with limited commercial terms, allowing many developers free use. Meta encourages the community to build and share projects using Muse Spark Open, which aims to democratize access to advanced AI models and promote safety research in the field.

entry.title: Researcher finds neural networks are inherently interpretable, challenging previous beliefs about polysemanticity and superposition in models like InceptionV1 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A researcher studying neural networks in image and language models has concluded that these networks are naturally clean and interpretable, contradicting earlier views that networks pack concepts arbitrarily through superposition. The study found that what was previously seen as complex entanglement was actually recursive generalization, and improvements in network architecture have made neurons more legible without changing model size or data. The research revisits canonical examples of polysemantic neurons, such as those in InceptionV1, and shows that architectural issues and weak interpretability tools caused misinterpretations. Modern language models also appear more interpretable than previously thought, suggesting that mechanistic interpretability can proceed directly on networks rather than relying on complex decompositions or reconstructions.

entry.title: Simons Foundation launches $15M initiative with Anthropic and OpenAI to support mathematicians adapting to AI tools and standards [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The Simons Foundation announced a $15 million partnership with Anthropic and OpenAI to help the mathematics community navigate the rise of artificial intelligence. The funding will support workshops, initiatives, and open calls for proposals aimed at evaluating AI-assisted results, sharing perspectives, and shaping standards for AI use in mathematics. Anthropic and OpenAI will also provide AI tools and computing resources to researchers supported by the foundation, extending support beyond mathematics to basic science. The initiative builds on the foundation's history of backing machine learning in science, including funding the Lean proof assistant, and aims to foster community-driven discussions on adopting and evaluating AI tools in mathematical research.

entry.title: Krea 3 launches as a production-ready image editing model offering precise, fast edits at $0.06 per image with native 2K resolution [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Krea 3 is a new image editing model designed for production use, enabling precise edits that change only specified areas of an image. It completes edits in about 8 seconds and costs approximately $0.06 per image, making it faster and cheaper than comparable models like Nano Banana Pro and GPT Image 2.5. The model supports up to eight reference images, hex color matching, and maintains character consistency across edits while rendering natively at 2K resolution. The model is aimed at creative professionals working on posters, branding, and covers, allowing users to swap elements while preserving layout and style. Krea 3 integrates with tools like Figma and Blender and offers features such as voice note editing and 251 launch presets. It is distributed through leading organizations and supports workflows involving image, video, and 3D models with single sign-on and intellectual property indemnification.

entry.title: Bold Agent Kit analysis finds human receptionists convert inbound calls four times better than AI despite AI handling more calls amid declining call center jobs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A new study by Bold Agent Kit analyzed approximately 14,000 inbound calls and found that human receptionists delivered about four times stronger conversion rates than AI agents, despite AI answering more calls. The research highlights that while AI reduces missed calls by about 15%, it experiences 700% more abandoned calls without meaningful progress, raising concerns about the effectiveness of AI in customer intake processes. The study reflects broader industry trends where call center employment growth has declined, possibly due to AI adoption, but suggests that AI's operational advantages in availability do not necessarily translate into better business outcomes. The findings emphasize the challenge businesses face in balancing AI automation with human interaction to optimize customer service and conversion rates.

entry.title: OpenAI updates ChatGPT Chrome extension to access and interact with users' open browser tabs for enhanced task automation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI has upgraded its ChatGPT Google Chrome extension to allow the AI to view and use information from users' open browser tabs when prompted through ChatGPT's web or desktop app. This feature enables ChatGPT to assist with tasks such as comparing products across tabs, filling out forms, drafting emails, and managing calendar events by leveraging the content of multiple open tabs. The extension also enhances ChatGPT's sidebar integration, providing full conversational capabilities and access to conversation history without leaving the current page. Additionally, ChatGPT Work can now control Chrome tabs to perform actions like sending messages, filling forms, downloading files, and organizing tabs, similar to Google's Gemini-powered auto browse feature.

entry.title: Linus Torvalds rejects banning AI in software development, calling such restrictions and their proponents 'stupid' [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Linus Torvalds criticized proposals to ban AI tools in kernel development, arguing that forbidding the use of certain tools is unreasonable and counterproductive. He compared banning AI to banning compilers or editors, emphasizing that understanding and competence matter more than the tools used. Torvalds stated that intelligent developers embrace new tools rather than avoid them, and he expects contributors to do their best regardless of the tools they employ.

entry.title: OpenAI launches Rosalind Academic Plan to provide eligible research labs free access to GPT-Rosalind and life sciences tools for up to 12 months [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI has introduced the Rosalind Academic Plan, offering eligible academic research labs sponsored access to GPT-Rosalind, a specialized AI model for life sciences, along with the Rosalind Workbench for scientific tool orchestration. The plan provides up to 30 Business Standard seats at no cost for up to one year, subject to trusted-access approval, aiming to accelerate foundational research in areas like drug design, genomics, and disease detection. The initiative supports academic scientists by combining their expertise with AI capabilities to advance discoveries in medicine, biotechnology, and related fields. Labs already using GPT-Rosalind report improvements in efficiency and scale for tasks such as protein design and neurodegeneration research. Data shared through the plan is not used to train OpenAI models by default, ensuring research privacy and integrity.

entry.title: Cal AI founder credits influencer strategy for viral growth and $30M revenue before MyFitness acquisition [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Cal AI, an AI-powered calorie tracking app founded in 2024 by 19-year-old Zach Yadegari, achieved viral success and generated over $30 million in revenue within two years by deploying a large network of influencers to promote the brand. The company was acquired by MyFitness in March for an undisclosed amount. Yadegari explained that paying influencers with targeted reach to post regularly created a predictable and rapid user growth formula. He also recently launched Persona, an AI agent startup focused on seamless computing integration, which has raised $10 million.

entry.title: Study finds AI fatigue among US healthcare engineers driven by pressure to evaluate new tools and manage AI alongside legacy systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A study of engineering and technology leaders in US healthcare reveals that AI fatigue is increasing due to constant pressure to assess emerging AI trends and the challenge of integrating AI-generated code with existing legacy systems. Nearly three-quarters of respondents feel pressured to evaluate every new AI tool despite limited capacity, while over half struggle to consistently assess AI technologies across governance and security requirements. The study suggests practical approaches to ease this strain, including focusing on organizational goals rather than every new trend, applying existing technology evaluation frameworks to AI tools, and conducting low-risk pilot tests with anonymized data. It also highlights different strategies for reviewing AI-generated code, from close pairing with language models to more hands-off "dim factory" approaches that balance oversight with developer workload. These findings underscore the need for realistic expectations, collaborative environments, and clear governance to manage AI adoption effectively.

entry.title: Google Antigravity platform accelerates discovery of novel antimicrobial peptides using AI-driven protein function prediction and structural analysis [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google has developed Antigravity, an agentic science workbench that streamlines the search for new antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) by integrating multiple databases and AI tools. Using ProtNLM, a deep learning model that predicts protein function from amino acid sequences, researchers identified a novel AMP candidate targeting respiratory pathogens, which is now undergoing laboratory validation. The platform enables researchers to interactively guide the AI agent through filtering millions of protein sequences, validating novelty against curated databases, and analyzing 3D protein structures with AlphaFold models. This approach addresses the urgent need for new antibiotics amid rising antimicrobial resistance by unlocking functional insights from uncharacterized protein sequences in global databases like UniProt.

entry.title: Linus Torvalds uses Anthropic's Claude Code AI to develop Linux kernel patches addressing memory cache slowdown [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Linus Torvalds has released a series of Linux kernel patches largely written with the help of Anthropic's Claude Code AI, targeting a memory cache contention issue that slows down multi-threaded reads. The patches aim to improve performance by deferring memory reuse until after a read-copy-update grace period, reducing processor core contention on shared cache lines. The improvements were tested on Torvalds's laptop, showing significant throughput gains in specific workloads, though the approach introduces trade-offs such as delayed memory reclamation and some regressions. As of mid-October 2026, the patches remain outside the mainline Linux kernel, with their future integration uncertain. Torvalds's use of AI marks a shift from skepticism to practical adoption in Linux development.

entry.title: Sega pulls Total War: Shogun 2 Complete Edition remaster from sale after launch issues with bugs and AI-upscaled visuals [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Sega has removed Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from digital storefronts following widespread user complaints about bugs and AI-upscaled graphics after its launch. The remaster, which includes the original game and all DLC with promised visual and control improvements, received overwhelmingly negative reviews on Steam and was quickly pulled from sale there. Sega and developer Creative Assembly acknowledged the problems and said they are working with their development partner to fix the issues and restore quality. They plan to reinstate the original game while allowing existing owners continued access to the Complete Edition. The developer Mataboo is also involved in the project.

entry.title: Mistral launches Timestral, a family of time-series foundation models with up to 209M parameters, leading benchmarks in probabilistic multivariate forecasting [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Mistral introduced Timestral, its first family of time-series foundation models designed for probabilistic, multivariate forecasting with models ranging from 5M to 209M parameters. Timestral outperforms larger models on key public benchmarks such as GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, while running efficiently on CPUs without requiring GPUs. The models support both past and known-future covariates and enable zero-shot forecasting across diverse domains.

entry.title: OpenAI launches AI for Educators course in Brazilian Portuguese and Study Mode feature to support active learning through guided questioning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI has introduced the AI for Educators course in Brazilian Portuguese on its free OpenAI Academy platform, aimed at helping teachers in primary, secondary, and higher education use AI to plan lessons and create activities while maintaining pedagogical judgment. Alongside this, OpenAI launched Study Mode in ChatGPT, a tool designed to promote active, step-by-step learning by asking students questions, providing hints, and checking understanding. Study Mode was developed with input from educators and experts to encourage reflection and reasoning, allowing students to engage deeply with subjects like biology or science through guided questioning. Teachers can also use the feature to assess student understanding and tailor classroom discussions. These tools were released on Teachers' Day 2026 to highlight the evolving role of educators in integrating AI into learning environments.

entry.title: Datadog launches Scout 1.0, an AI model specialized for investigating production issues with lower inference costs and improved efficiency [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Datadog has introduced Scout 1.0, its first AI model designed specifically to investigate production issues and power its Bits Investigation AI SRE tool. Scout 1.0 aims to reduce inference costs significantly, enabling more frequent and earlier investigations during incidents while maintaining competitive performance compared to other models. The model was trained using reinforcement learning on realistic simulations built from historical incidents and telemetry data without using customer data. Scout 1.0 is currently in closed preview with select customers and Datadog engineering teams using it to investigate production alerts. The model supports Bits as an always-on first responder that gathers evidence and identifies likely causes before engineers intervene, reducing on-call workload and enabling deeper investigations. Datadog plans to continue improving Scout's investigation quality and cost efficiency, with future goals to extend its capabilities toward autonomous issue remediation to accelerate incident resolution and further reduce operational burdens.

entry.title: Trump posts AI-edited photo of White House column restoration on Truth Social, flagged by Google's AI detector [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: President Donald Trump shared a series of photos on Truth Social showcasing White House renovations, including one image of a column that appears to have been altered using AI. The AI-edited photo, which compares an old column to a "restored" one, shows inconsistencies such as mismatched steps and nearly identical angles, and was flagged by Google's SynthID Detector as created or edited with OpenAI technology. Other photos posted by Trump showing the White House facade and heliport were not flagged, and real images from June show people painting the White House exterior, suggesting some restoration work did occur. The White House has not responded to requests for comment on the AI-edited image, while Trump has a history of posting AI-generated content.

entry.title: Why AI-Written Software Needs a Flight Simulator [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: As companies create more applications using AI, corporate officers say demand is rising for a new type of software that stress-tests those apps, simulating how they handle network problems and other disasters that humans may not think to test for-including cyberattacks by rogue AIs. Luis Chávez, CTO of coding assistant provider Replit, says his company uses an AI-assisted software known as a deterministic simulator, a kind of flight simulator for software. The deterministic part refers to how the simulator lets companies run the same disaster test again and again so they can try out different fixes for bugs that crop up during network failures or hacking attempts. Traditional stress-testing methods rely on developers guessing every potential problem that may arise. Merely using today's AI models to evaluate code often produces false alarms or fake warnings, corporate executives say.

Cursor, the AI coding startup SpaceX was then in the process of acquiring, was developing Grok Bot, and as part of that process, employees across Cursor were using the tool extensively for testing and as a part of their everyday work. In late July, engineers raised concerns that Cursor might have sent data from that internal testing-potentially including confidential information about its customers, suppliers and business partners-to SpaceX's AI unit. entry.title: Cognition's Plan to Limit Tokenmaxxing to the Most Efficient Engineers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: To rein in AI spending, large companies are capping employees' usage, turning to cheaper and smaller models and using routers to send only the hardest requests to the most expensive models. Cognition, the startup behind the AI coding agent Devin, is adding a new trick to the book: measuring how efficiently different engineers use AI so companies can allocate more resources toward their most efficient employees, Cognition told The Information exclusively. "The limits that a user should have should not be static. They should be dynamic based on the efficiency of your usage and the value that you're getting out of it," said Calvin Giroud, a vice president of customer engineering at Cognition. By looking at an engineer's coding session using Devin, Cognition can estimate the equivalent number of hours it would have taken a human to do the same amount of work. Dividing by the costs of that session, Cognition gets a measure of each engineer's efficiency.

entry.title: Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO The phrase "told investors" appears four times in this FT article, which reports on Anthropic's day of hosting investors on Wednesday. Lots of details in here from "people with knowledge of the matter". Key things I learned from the article: Q1 revenue (Jan/Feb/Mar) was "about $4.8bn" Q2 (Apr/May/Jun) was $11.5bn Q3 (Jul/Aug/Sep) was $16.8bn In Q3: $1.70 in revenue for every $1 spent on "computing power" Adjusted operating margins (excluding stock-based compensation) were 11% This point about distillation is worth quoting in full (highlight mine): The start-up has also clamped down on "distillation" - a controversial practice whereby rival AI labs train their models on the outputs of more advanced ones. When rival companies "distil" their models from Anthropic's models, that involves heavy usage and spending. Anthropic told investors on Wednesday distillation accounted for 5 per cent to 7 per cent of revenue and that they had cut it back "materially" in the third quarter of the year, said four people with direct knowledge of the matter. Napkin maths says that if distillation was 5% of their Q2 revenue (before they cut it back in Q3) then unnamed "other labs" spent over half a billion dollars distilling Anthropic's models in that quarter! Also notable: Anthropic appear to no longer be leaning on "annualized run-rate revenue" (previously) in these communications to their investors. Tags: ai, generative-ai, llms, anthropic
